title: Daily Electone Practice at Home
html:
Unlike the piano or keyboard, the Electone is an electronic organ designed to simulate the dynamics of an entire orchestra.

It is a console of multiple manuals and foot pedals, where both hands and feet collaborate to layer melody, harmony, and rhythm simultaneously.

It challenges the linearity of performance:
The upper manual plays melodies or leads,
The lower manual carries harmony or counterpoint,
The pedals add bass or rhythm, anchoring the whole composition.

This multi-dimensionality makes the Electone less about reproducing piano music and more about orchestral imagination in real time.

It is an instrument of arrangement, layering, and improvisation, where the performer is also the conductor of textures.

For me, the Electone resonates with my fascination for composition as method:
like the city, it demands coordination between different registers, scales, and rhythms.

It is not about mastering one line of sound but orchestrating multiplicity into coherence.

title: Listening to Everything
html:
Listening has never been only about music,
never confined to a single genre.
I used to sit quietly in the park,
letting the environment play its own score: wind, footsteps, distant voices.

I remain grateful for hearing,
even if I cannot live,
especially sleep, without earplugs.
Gratitude and fragility arrive together,
reminding me that listening
is both gift and practice.

title: Reading Not for Anything
html:
Reading drifts between many shelves,
from textbooks and essays
to popular fiction picked up for pure pleasure.

It shapes understanding in unexpected ways,
fostering both curiosity and empathy.
Not for purpose, not for achievement, simply for the act of entering other worlds.

title: Learning Korean
html:
Korean came through music first,
lines of lyrics sung into memory.
Now it grows through daily practice,
another rhythm of listening and repeating,
a language that opens new voices.

title: Exploring the World
html:
Travel has been with me since childhood,
first on family trips across the country,
later on journeys abroad during college.

I think I simply enjoy being elsewhere, seeing how streets, voices, and skies
shift from place to place,
each moment carrying its own rhythm of arrival.

title: My little Balcony Garden
html:
→ Explore the full Fun with Flowers experiment

Balcony gardening began as a small experiment,
an echo of my grandparents long ago.
It started with five sunflower seeds,
a pot on the window ledge leaning toward the sun.

Soon the space became a quiet companion,
teaching patience through soil and leaves.

Each sprout is a reminder
that growth can happen in miniature,
and that even a narrow ledge
can open into a garden.

title: P5.JS Interactive Experiment
html:
→ Explore the full Field of Forms experiment

I spent the evening tracing invisible stems.

Each drag left a trail of petals that breathed, faded, and reappeared,
as if the screen remembered every motion.
It was my first brushset in p5.js,
a Field of Forms growing from code and chance.

The shapes oscillated between control and accident.
They carried the rhythm of my hand, the echo of my own hesitation.
Every color lingered, every sound a delayed pulse,
a tiny act of composition between the mechanical and the organic.

What began as debugging a trail became a quiet garden of gestures.
Not perfect, but alive enough to hum when silence fell.

Maybe that’s all I wanted:
to let code remember what touch forgets.

title: Creating Zines
html:
Zine-making slips into the everyday: pages filled with fragments, collages,
scraps of mood and memory.
It felt like a pocket-sized stage
for sketches, notes, and fragments of thought.

Sometimes it turns toward fandom,
a way of keeping songs, lyrics, and characters close.
Each zine feels like a diary in disguise,
private and playful at once.

title: Practicing Watercolor
html:
Watercolour is a practice in both control and uncontrol.
The brush teaches how water carries colour,
sometimes precise, sometimes drifting freely.

I found that letting it wander was also part of the joy,
as if the page itself joined the act of painting.

title: Working with Leather
html:
When I was young, I tried knitting a scarf,
though my mother’s hands carried the skill better than mine.
Years later in a fine art class,
I turned to leather, dense with weight and labor,
where resistance and softness meet.

Cutting, stitching, bending,
the process unfolded slowly, with its own rhythm,
teaching that making is as much about patience
as it is about form.

title: Exploring Digital Art
html:
Watching my roommate create fantastic art,
I began learning digital art on my own.
Each piece feels like a wonder, a play with pixels and codes instead of ink,
layers and operators instead of paper.

Undo becomes part of the process,
textures stretch beyond the page,
yet I still search for an image
that breathes with presence.

title: The Art of Calligraphy
guidance: Script in the Copperplate Style by Dr. Joseph M. Vitolo
html:
The dream of calligraphy began at 12,
but it wasn’t until 2023 that I truly entered the practice and found peace in its rhythm.
Delving into the graceful art of calligraphy, exploring its history, techniques, and the meditative process of creating beautiful letters.

title: Animating Everything
html:
Learning to animate everything, letting motion make images playful: merchandise, logos, vlogs, fragments of daily life.

Letters scatter, shapes collide, flowers sway, moments stretch and fold into rhythm.

Each attempt is a discovery,
showing how the simplest gesture
can bring static things to life.
